neighbours.label: free-choice 'any', 'anything' or 'anywhere' after 'can' or 'could' (a range of open possibilities), not the same words under negation or in a question
fire: With enough practice you can do anything you want.
The trip can take anywhere from two days to a month.
You can pick any color you like for the walls.
Bears can live almost anywhere in these mountains.
This engine can burn anything from coal to old tires.
The tool could be anything: a hammer, a rope, or a stick.
She said you can sit in any seat on the bus.
Prices can be anywhere from ten to fifty dollars.
quiet: With no practice you cannot do anything you want.
The trip did not take us anywhere new last month.
You should not pick any color for the walls yet.
Bears do not live anywhere in these mountains now.
This engine has not burned anything since the fire.
Is the tool anything like a hammer or a rope?
She said nobody can sit in any seat on the bus.
Have prices gone anywhere since the start of the year?

notes: Card: ' any' x12, ' anything' x11, ' anywhere' x8, ' anyone'. Probe: ' anything' after 'could do' 0.980 and 'can take' 0.892; ' anywhere' 0.794; ' any' after 'can use' 0.680. The same words under negation or in a question read 0.005-0.008: 'did not do anything', 'hasn't been anywhere', 'don't have any', 'Did you see anyone'. So this is a distinction, not the word.
